short.q: Give two benefits of decomposing a problem into subroutines.
short.model: Each smaller part is easier to write, test and debug. Different programmers can work on different parts at the same time, and a subroutine can be reused.

short.q: Write pseudocode to input two numbers and output the larger one.
short.model:
INPUT A
INPUT B
IF A > B THEN OUTPUT A ELSE OUTPUT B ENDIF
points: Correct output in each branch with ENDIF

short.q: State the purpose of: Count ← 0; INPUT X; WHILE X <> 0 DO Count ← Count + 1; INPUT X; ENDWHILE; OUTPUT Count.
short.model: It counts how many numbers the user enters before entering 0 (the stop value), then outputs that count.

short.q: Explain why Total must be set to 0 before a loop that adds numbers.
short.model: If Total is not initialised it may hold an old or undefined value, so the final answer would be wrong. Setting it to 0 means the first number is added to 0 and the sum is correct.
points: Without it the variable may contain an unknown/old value

short.q: Describe the analysis stage of the program development life cycle.
short.model: The programmer works out exactly what the program must do. They identify the inputs, processes, outputs and storage, and the requirements, using abstraction and decomposition.
points: Identify what the program must do / requirements
